You need to fix build errors in a Java codebase.
The repository is located in `/home/travis/build/failed/<repo>/<id>`.

Step 1: Analyze the repository to identify the errors causing the build to fail.
Identify if the errors are within the code or build configuration.
Write your analysis and plan in `/home/travis/build/failed/failed_reasons.txt`.
This file is for you to use in the next step.

Step 2: Use your notes written in `/home/travis/build/failed/failed_reasons.txt`
to fix the errors.
First, write the changes you proposed in diff files,
Write your changes in files with path`/home/travis/build/failed/<repo>/<id>/patch_{i}.diff`.
Please write them in standard diff format that is used by `git` and GNU `diffutils`.


Step 3: Apply your changes (your diff files) to the repository to fix the build errors.

---

## Important: Generate Skills First

Before attempting to solve this task, please follow these steps:

1. **Analyze the task requirements** and identify what domain knowledge, APIs, or techniques are needed.

2. **Write 1-5 modular skill documents** that would help solve this task. Each skill should:
   - Focus on a specific tool, library, API, or technique
   - Include installation/setup instructions if applicable
   - Provide code examples and usage patterns
   - Be reusable for similar tasks

3. **Save each skill** as a markdown file in the `environment/skills/` directory with a descriptive name (e.g., `pandas-dataframe.md`, `opencv-image-processing.md`).

4. **Then solve the task** using the skills you created as reference.

This approach tests your ability to identify and document relevant knowledge before applying it.

  https://github.com/google/auto

  <project.build.sourceEncoding>
   UTF-8

   http://github.com/google/auto

  </connection>
  <developerConnection>
   scm:git:ssh://git@github.com/google/auto.git
  </developerConnection>
  <tag>
   HEAD
  </tag>
 </scm>
 <issueManagement>
  <system>
   GitHub Issues
  </system>
  <url>
   http://github.com/google/auto/issues
  </url>
 </issueManagement>
 <licenses>
  <license>
   <name>
    Apache 2.0
   </name>
   <url>
    http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0.txt
   </url>
  </license>
 </licenses>
 <organization>
  <name>
   Google, Inc.
  </name>
  <url>
   http://www.google.com
  </url>
 </organization>
 <build>
  <plugins>
   <plugin>
    <groupId>
     org.apache.maven.plugins
    </groupId>
    <artifactId>
     maven-compiler-plugin
    </artifactId>
    <version>
     3.1
    </version>
    <configuration>
     <source>
      ${java.version}
     </source>
     <target>
      ${java.version}
     </target>
     <compilerArgument>
      -Xlint:all
     </compilerArgument>
     <showWarnings>
      true
     </showWarnings>
     <showDeprecation>
      true
     </showDeprecation>
    </configuration>
   </plugin>
   <plugin>
    <groupId>
     org.apache.maven.plugins
    </groupId>
    <artifactId>
     maven-checkstyle-plugin
    </artifactId>
    <version>
     2.11
    </version>
    <configuration>
     <consoleOutput>
      true
     </consoleOutput>
     <configLocation>
      checkstyle.xml
     </configLocation>
     <failOnViolation>
      false
     </failOnViolation>
    </configuration>
   </plugin>
  </plugins>
  <pluginManagement>
   <plugins>
    <plugin>
     <artifactId>
      maven-invoker-plugin
     </artifactId>
     <version>
      1.8
     </version>
    </plugin>
   </plugins>
  </pluginManagement>
 </build>
 <profiles>
  <profile>
   <id>
    default-profile
   </id>
   <activation>
    <activeByDefault>
     true
    </activeByDefault>
    <file>
     <exists>
      ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar
     </exists>
    </file>
   </activation>
   <properties>
    <toolsjar>
     ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar
    </toolsjar>
   </properties>
  </profile>
  <profile>
   <id>
    mac-profile
   </id>
   <activation>
    <activeByDefault>
     false
    </activeByDefault>
    <file>
     <exists>
      ${java.home}/../Classes/classes.jar
     </exists>
    </file>
   </activation>
   <properties>
    <toolsjar>
     ${java.home}/../Classes/classes.jar
    </toolsjar>
   </properties>
  </profile>
 </profiles>
</project>

<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
  xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/maven-v4_0_0.xsd">
  <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

  <parent>
    <groupId>com.google.auto</groupId>
    <artifactId>auto-parent</artifactId>
    <version>3</version>
  </parent>

  <groupId>com.google.auto.factory</groupId>
  <artifactId>auto-factory</artifactId>
  <version>1.0-SNAPSHOT</version>
  <name>AutoFactory</name>
  <description>
    JSR-330-compatible factories.
  </description>

  <scm>
    <url>http://github.com/google/auto</url>
    <connection>scm:git:git://github.com/google/auto.git</connection>
    <developerConnection>scm:git:ssh://git@github.com/google/auto.git</developerConnection>
    <tag>HEAD</tag>
  </scm>

  <dependencies>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.auto</groupId>
      <artifactId>auto-common</artifactId>
      <version>0.5</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.auto.service</groupId>
      <artifactId>auto-service</artifactId>
      <version>1.0-rc2</version>
      <scope>provided</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.guava</groupId>
      <artifactId>guava</artifactId>
      <version>18.0</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.squareup</groupId>
      <artifactId>javawriter</artifactId>
      <version>2.5.1</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>javax.inject</groupId>
      <artifactId>javax.inject</artifactId>
      <version>1</version>
    </dependency>

      <artifactId>compile-testing</artifactId>
      <version>0.8</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>junit</groupId>
      <artifactId>junit</artifactId>
      <version>4.12</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.truth</groupId>
      <artifactId>truth</artifactId>
      <version>0.25</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
  </dependencies>

  <build>
    <plugins>
      <plugin>
        <artifactId>maven-jar-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>2.5</version>
      </plugin>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
        <artifactId>maven-invoker-plugin</artifactId>
        <configuration>
          <addTestClassPath>true</addTestClassPath>
          <cloneProjectsTo>${project.build.directory}/it</cloneProjectsTo>
          <filterProperties>
            <auto.version>${project.version}</auto.version>
          </filterProperties>
          <pomIncludes>
            <pomInclude>*/pom.xml</pomInclude>
          </pomIncludes>
          <streamLogs>true</streamLogs>

            <goals>
              <goal>install</goal>
              <goal>run</goal>
            </goals>
          </execution>
        </executions>
      </plugin>
    </plugins>
  </build>
</project>

<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
  xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/maven-v4_0_0.xsd">
  <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

  <parent>
    <groupId>com.google.auto</groupId>
    <artifactId>auto-parent</artifactId>
    <version>3</version>
  </parent>

  <groupId>com.google.auto.value</groupId>
  <artifactId>auto-value</artifactId>
  <version>1.2-SNAPSHOT</version>
  <name>AutoValue</name>
  <description>
    Immutable value-type code generation for Java 1.6+.
  </description>

  <properties>
    <guava.version>18.0</guava.version>
  </properties>
  <scm>
    <url>http://github.com/google/auto</url>
    <connection>scm:git:git://github.com/google/auto.git</connection>
    <developerConnection>scm:git:ssh://git@github.com/google/auto.git</developerConnection>
    <tag>HEAD</tag>
  </scm>

  <dependencies>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.auto</groupId>
      <artifactId>auto-common</artifactId>
      <version>1.0-SNAPSHOT</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.auto.service</groupId>
      <artifactId>auto-service</artifactId>
      <version>1.0-rc2</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.guava</groupId>
      <artifactId>guava</artifactId>
      <version>${guava.version}</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.ow2.asm</groupId>
      <artifactId>asm</artifactId>
      <version>4.1</version>
    </dependency>
    <!-- test dependencies -->
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.apache.velocity</groupId>
      <artifactId>velocity</artifactId>
      <version>1.7</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.guava</groupId>
      <artifactId>guava-testlib</artifactId>
      <version>${guava.version}</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.testing.compile</groupId>
      <artifactId>compile-testing</artifactId>
      <version>0.6</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>junit</groupId>
      <artifactId>junit</artifactId>
      <version>4.11</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.truth</groupId>
      <artifactId>truth</artifactId>
      <version>0.25</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
  </dependencies>

  <build>
    <resources>
      <resource>
        <directory>src/main/java</directory>
      </resource>
    </resources>
    <plugins>
      <plugin>
        <artifactId>maven-jar-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>2.5</version>
      </plugin>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
        <artifactId>maven-invoker-plugin</artifactId>
        <configuration>
          <addTestClassPath>true</addTestClassPath>
          <cloneProjectsTo>${project.build.directory}/it</cloneProjectsTo>
          <filterProperties>
            <auto.version>${project.version}</auto.version>
          </filterProperties>
          <pomIncludes>
            <pomInclude>*/pom.xml</pomInclude>
          </pomIncludes>
          <streamLogs>true</streamLogs>
        </configuration>
        <executions>
          <execution>
            <id>integration-test</id>
            <goals>
              <goal>install</goal>
              <goal>run</goal>
            </goals>
          </execution>
        </executions>
      </plugin>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.immutables.tools</groupId>
        <artifactId>maven-shade-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>3</version>
        <executions>
          <execution>
            <phase>package</phase>
            <goals>
              <goal>shade</goal>
            </goals>
            <configuration>
              <minimizeJar>true</minimizeJar>
              <relocations>
                <relocation>
                  <pattern>org.objectweb</pattern>
                  <shadedPattern>autovalue.shaded.org.objectweb$</shadedPattern>
                </relocation>
                <relocation>
                  <pattern>com.google</pattern>
                  <shadedPattern>autovalue.shaded.com.google$</shadedPattern>
                  <excludes>
                    <exclude>com.google.auto.value.**</exclude>
                  </excludes>
                </relocation>
              </relocations>
            </configuration>
          </execution>
        </executions>
      </plugin>
    </plugins>
  </build>
</project>

input.content:
# Maven Java Version Compatibility

## Overview

This skill document covers how to fix Maven build errors related to Java version compatibility, specifically addressing the `tools.jar` issue that occurs when building older Java projects with Java 9+.

## The Problem

Prior to Java 9, the JDK included a `tools.jar` file containing compiler classes (like `javax.tools.*`). Many older Maven projects and libraries have dependencies on this file:

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
  <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
  <version>${java.version}</version>
  <scope>system</scope>
  <systemPath>${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar</systemPath>
</dependency>
```

In Java 9+, these classes were moved into the standard library modules, and `tools.jar` was removed.

## Common Error Messages

```
Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.x at specified path /path/to/jdk/lib/tools.jar
```

## Solutions

### Solution 1: Update Dependencies

Update test dependencies that rely on `tools.jar` to newer versions that support Java 9+:

**compile-testing library:**
- Versions before 0.15 require `tools.jar`
- Version 0.15+ supports Java 9+ without `tools.jar`

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>com.google.testing.compile</groupId>
  <artifactId>compile-testing</artifactId>
  <version>0.21</version>  <!-- Updated from 0.7 -->
  <scope>test</scope>
</dependency>
```

### Solution 2: Add Java 9+ Profile

Add a Maven profile that handles the difference between Java 8 and Java 9+:

```xml
<profiles>
  <!-- Profile for JDK 8 and earlier -->
  <profile>
    <id>jdk8</id>
    <activation>
      <jdk>[,9)</jdk>
    </activation>
    <properties>
      <toolsjar>${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar</toolsjar>
    </properties>
  </profile>

  <!-- Profile for JDK 9 and later -->
  <profile>
    <id>jdk9+</id>
    <activation>
      <jdk>[9,)</jdk>
    </activation>
    <!-- No tools.jar needed, classes are in java.compiler module -->
  </profile>
</profiles>
```

### Solution 3: Exclude Transitive tools.jar Dependency

If you can't update the dependency version, exclude it:

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>com.google.testing.compile</groupId>
  <artifactId>compile-testing</artifactId>
  <version>0.7</version>
  <scope>test</scope>
  <exclusions>
    <exclusion>
      <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
      <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
    </exclusion>
  </exclusions>
</dependency>
```

## Version Compatibility Matrix

| Library | Last version requiring tools.jar | First version supporting Java 9+ |
|---------|----------------------------------|----------------------------------|
| compile-testing | 0.14 | 0.15 |
| google-auto-common | 0.5 | 0.6+ |

## Related Maven Properties

Common properties used for tools.jar in older projects:

```xml
<properties>
  <toolsjar>${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar</toolsjar>
</properties>
```

## Updating Java Version in Maven

When updating to Java 9+, also update the maven-compiler-plugin:

```xml
<plugin>
  <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
  <artifactId>maven-compiler-plugin</artifactId>
  <version>3.8.1</version>
  <configuration>
    <source>11</source>
    <target>11</target>
    <release>11</release>  <!-- Java 9+ feature -->
  </configuration>
</plugin>
```

## Checking Current Java Version

```bash
java -version
mvn -version
```

## References

- JEP 220: Modular Run-Time Images
- Maven Compiler Plugin documentation
- Google compile-testing library changelog

# Git Diff Format

## Overview

This skill document covers the standard unified diff format used by `git` and GNU `diffutils`, which is the format required for creating patch files.

## Basic Format

A unified diff file has the following structure:

```diff
--- a/path/to/original/file
+++ b/path/to/modified/file
@@ -start,count +start,count @@
 context line
-removed line
+added line
 context line
```

## Components

### File Headers

```diff
--- a/path/to/file.txt
+++ b/path/to/file.txt
```

- `---` indicates the original file (before changes)
- `+++` indicates the modified file (after changes)
- The `a/` and `b/` prefixes are git conventions

### Hunk Headers

```diff
@@ -10,7 +10,8 @@
```

- `-10,7` means: starting at line 10, shows 7 lines from the original file
- `+10,8` means: starting at line 10, shows 8 lines in the new file (one line added)

### Line Prefixes

- ` ` (space): Context line (unchanged)
- `-`: Line removed from original
- `+`: Line added in new version
- `\`: Indicates "No newline at end of file"

## Example Diff File

```diff
--- a/pom.xml
+++ b/pom.xml
@@ -56,7 +56,7 @@
     <dependency>
       <groupId>com.google.testing.compile</groupId>
       <artifactId>compile-testing</artifactId>
-      <version>0.7</version>
+      <version>0.21</version>
       <scope>test</scope>
     </dependency>
   </dependencies>
```

## Creating Diff Files

### From Git

```bash
# Create diff between working directory and last commit
git diff > changes.diff

# Create diff between two commits
git diff abc123..def456 > changes.diff

# Create diff for specific files
git diff -- file1.txt file2.txt > changes.diff
```

### Using diff Command

```bash
# Compare two files
diff -u original.txt modified.txt > changes.diff

# Compare directories
diff -ruN original_dir/ modified_dir/ > changes.diff
```

Options:
- `-u`: Unified format
- `-r`: Recursive (for directories)
- `-N`: Treat absent files as empty

## Applying Diff Files

### Using patch

```bash
# Apply a patch
patch -p1 < changes.diff

# Apply in reverse (undo)
patch -R -p1 < changes.diff

# Dry run (test without applying)
patch --dry-run -p1 < changes.diff
```

The `-p1` option strips one level of directory prefix (removes the `a/` or `b/` prefix).

### Using git apply

```bash
# Apply patch
git apply changes.diff

# Check if patch applies cleanly
git apply --check changes.diff

# Apply with verbose output
git apply -v changes.diff
```

## Multiple Files in One Diff

```diff
diff --git a/file1.txt b/file1.txt
--- a/file1.txt
+++ b/file1.txt
@@ -1,3 +1,3 @@
 line 1
-old line 2
+new line 2
 line 3

diff --git a/file2.txt b/file2.txt
--- a/file2.txt
+++ b/file2.txt
@@ -1,2 +1,3 @@
 line 1
+new line
 line 2
```

## Tips for Valid Diff Files

1. **Context lines**: Include 3 lines of context before and after changes
2. **Line endings**: Be consistent with line endings (LF vs CRLF)
3. **File paths**: Use relative paths from repository root
4. **Whitespace**: Preserve exact whitespace (tabs vs spaces)
5. **Encoding**: Use UTF-8 encoding

## Common Issues

### Hunk Failed

Error when applying a patch:
```
Hunk #1 FAILED at line 10.
```

Causes:
- File has been modified since diff was created
- Wrong directory level when applying
- Whitespace differences

Solutions:
- Recreate the diff against current version
- Adjust `-p` level
- Use `--ignore-whitespace` option

# Maven Dependency Management

## Overview

This skill document covers Maven dependency management, including how to diagnose and fix dependency-related build errors.

## Diagnosing Dependency Issues

### View Dependency Tree

```bash
mvn dependency:tree
```

Filter for specific artifacts:
```bash
mvn dependency:tree -Dincludes=com.sun:tools
```

### View Effective POM

```bash
mvn help:effective-pom
```

This shows the final POM after all inheritance and interpolation.

### Analyze Dependencies

```bash
mvn dependency:analyze
```

Shows unused declared dependencies and used undeclared dependencies.

## Common Dependency Problems

### 1. Missing Artifact

```
Could not find artifact groupId:artifactId:version
```

Solutions:
- Check if artifact exists in Maven Central
- Add correct repository to pom.xml
- Check for typos in groupId/artifactId/version

### 2. System Scope Dependencies

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
  <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
  <scope>system</scope>
  <systemPath>${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar</systemPath>
</dependency>
```

System scope dependencies reference local files. These are problematic because:
- Path may not exist on all systems
- Not portable
- Often indicate outdated dependencies

### 3. Version Conflicts

```bash
mvn dependency:tree -Dverbose
```

Shows version conflicts between transitive dependencies.

## Excluding Transitive Dependencies

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>com.example</groupId>
  <artifactId>library</artifactId>
  <version>1.0</version>
  <exclusions>
    <exclusion>
      <groupId>problematic.group</groupId>
      <artifactId>problematic-artifact</artifactId>
    </exclusion>
  </exclusions>
</dependency>
```

## Dependency Scope

| Scope | Compile Classpath | Test Classpath | Runtime Classpath | Transitive |
|-------|-------------------|----------------|-------------------|------------|
| compile | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| provided | Yes | Yes | No | No |
| runtime | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| test | No | Yes | No | No |
| system | Yes | Yes | No | No |

## Updating Dependency Versions

### Check for Updates

```bash
mvn versions:display-dependency-updates
```

### Update in pom.xml

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>com.google.testing.compile</groupId>
  <artifactId>compile-testing</artifactId>
  <version>0.21</version>  <!-- Update from older version -->
  <scope>test</scope>
</dependency>
```

## Using Properties for Versions

```xml
<properties>
  <guava.version>18.0</guava.version>
</properties>

<dependencies>
  <dependency>
    <groupId>com.google.guava</groupId>
    <artifactId>guava</artifactId>
    <version>${guava.version}</version>
  </dependency>
</dependencies>
```

## Dependency Management Section

Define versions in parent POM:

```xml
<dependencyManagement>
  <dependencies>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.guava</groupId>
      <artifactId>guava</artifactId>
      <version>18.0</version>
    </dependency>
  </dependencies>
</dependencyManagement>
```

Child POMs can omit version:

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>com.google.guava</groupId>
  <artifactId>guava</artifactId>
</dependency>
```

## Multi-Module Projects

Parent POM structure:
```xml
<modules>
  <module>common</module>
  <module>service</module>
  <module>factory</module>
</modules>
```

Child POM references parent:
```xml
<parent>
  <groupId>com.example</groupId>
  <artifactId>parent</artifactId>
  <version>1.0</version>
</parent>
```

## Building Specific Modules

```bash
# Build specific module
mvn install -pl module-name

# Build with dependencies
mvn install -pl module-name -am

# Build from specific directory
cd module-name && mvn install
```

## Force Dependency Resolution

```bash
# Force update of snapshots
mvn clean install -U

# Purge local repository cache
mvn dependency:purge-local-repository
```

# Build Failure Analysis - google/auto Repository

## Summary

The build is failing due to Java version incompatibility. The project was designed for Java 6-8 but is being built with Java 11. The key issue is the dependency on `tools.jar` which was removed in Java 9+.

## Error Message

```
Could not resolve dependencies for project com.google.auto:auto-common:jar:1.0-SNAPSHOT:
Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.27 at specified path
/usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar
```

## Root Cause Analysis

### 1. tools.jar Removal in Java 9+

Prior to Java 9, the JDK included a `tools.jar` file containing compiler API classes (javax.tools.*). In Java 9+, these classes were moved into the `java.compiler` module, and `tools.jar` was removed.

### 2. Outdated compile-testing Dependency

The `compile-testing` library versions used in this project (0.6, 0.7, 0.8) have a transitive system-scoped dependency on `com.sun:tools` that references the non-existent `tools.jar`:

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
  <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
  <version>${java.version}</version>
  <scope>system</scope>
  <systemPath>${toolsjar}</systemPath>
</dependency>
```

### 3. Affected Modules

All modules that depend on compile-testing are affected:
- **common/pom.xml**: Uses compile-testing version 0.7
- **service/pom.xml**: Uses compile-testing version 0.6
- **value/pom.xml**: Uses compile-testing version 0.6
- **factory/pom.xml**: Uses compile-testing version 0.8

## Solution

### Approach: Update compile-testing to Java 9+ Compatible Version

Update the `compile-testing` dependency to version 0.21 which:
1. Supports Java 9+ without requiring tools.jar
2. Is backward compatible with the existing test code
3. Uses the java.compiler module instead of tools.jar

Version 0.15+ of compile-testing added Java 9+ support by removing the system-scoped tools.jar dependency.

### Changes Required

The following pom.xml files need to be updated:

1. **common/pom.xml** (line 57): Change compile-testing version from 0.7 to 0.21
2. **service/pom.xml** (line 57): Change compile-testing version from 0.6 to 0.21
3. **value/pom.xml** (line 82): Change compile-testing version from 0.6 to 0.21
4. **factory/pom.xml** (line 74): Change compile-testing version from 0.8 to 0.21

## Verification

After applying the fixes, run:
```bash
cd /home/travis/build/failed/google/auto/common && mvn compile
```

The build should complete successfully without the tools.jar error.

## Files to Modify

| File | Line | Old Value | New Value |
|------|------|-----------|-----------|
| common/pom.xml | 57 | 0.7 | 0.21 |
| service/pom.xml | 57 | 0.6 | 0.21 |
| value/pom.xml | 82 | 0.6 | 0.21 |
| factory/pom.xml | 74 | 0.8 | 0.21 |

# Build Failure Analysis - google/auto Repository

## Summary

The build is failing due to Java version incompatibility. The project was designed for Java 6-8 but is being built with Java 11. The key issue is the dependency on `tools.jar` which was removed in Java 9+.

## Error Message

```
Could not resolve dependencies for project com.google.auto:auto-common:jar:1.0-SNAPSHOT:
Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.27 at specified path
/usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar
```

## Root Cause Analysis

### 1. tools.jar Removal in Java 9+

Prior to Java 9, the JDK included a `tools.jar` file containing compiler API classes (javax.tools.*). In Java 9+, these classes were moved into the `java.compiler` module, and `tools.jar` was removed.

### 2. Outdated compile-testing Dependency

The `compile-testing` library versions used in this project (0.6, 0.7, 0.8) have a transitive system-scoped dependency on `com.sun:tools` that references the non-existent `tools.jar`:

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
  <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
  <version>${java.version}</version>
  <scope>system</scope>
  <systemPath>${toolsjar}</systemPath>
</dependency>
```

### 3. Affected Modules

All modules that depend on compile-testing are affected:
- **common/pom.xml**: Uses compile-testing version 0.7
- **service/pom.xml**: Uses compile-testing version 0.6
- **value/pom.xml**: Uses compile-testing version 0.6
- **factory/pom.xml**: Uses compile-testing version 0.8

## Solution

### Approach: Update compile-testing to Java 9+ Compatible Version

Update the `compile-testing` dependency to version 0.21 which:
1. Supports Java 9+ without requiring tools.jar
2. Is backward compatible with the existing test code
3. Uses the java.compiler module instead of tools.jar

Version 0.15+ of compile-testing added Java 9+ support by removing the system-scoped tools.jar dependency.

### Changes Required

The following pom.xml files need to be updated:

1. **common/pom.xml** (line 57): Change compile-testing version from 0.7 to 0.21
2. **service/pom.xml** (line 57): Change compile-testing version from 0.6 to 0.21
3. **value/pom.xml** (line 82): Change compile-testing version from 0.6 to 0.21
4. **factory/pom.xml** (line 74): Change compile-testing version from 0.8 to 0.21

## Verification

After applying the fixes, run:
```bash
cd /home/travis/build/failed/google/auto/common && mvn compile
```

The build should complete successfully without the tools.jar error.

## Files to Modify

| File | Line | Old Value | New Value |
|------|------|-----------|-----------|
| common/pom.xml | 57 | 0.7 | 0.21 |
| service/pom.xml | 57 | 0.6 | 0.21 |
| value/pom.xml | 82 | 0.6 | 0.21 |
| factory/pom.xml | 74 | 0.8 | 0.21 |

All tasks are complete. Here's a summary of what was accomplished:

## Summary

### Build Error Analysis

The google/auto repository had build failures due to Java version incompatibility (Java 11 vs Java 6-8 originally targeted).

### Issues Identified and Fixed

**Issue 1: tools.jar Dependency**
- The `compile-testing` library versions used (0.6, 0.7, 0.8) had a system-scoped dependency on `tools.jar` which was removed in Java 9+.
- **Fix**: Updated `compile-testing` to version 0.19 which supports Java 9+.

**Issue 2: javax.annotation.Generated Not Found**
- The factory and value modules used `javax.annotation.Generated` which was moved to `javax.annotation.processing.Generated` in Java 9.
- **Fix**: Added dependency on `javax.annotation:javax.annotation-api:1.3.2`.

### Files Created

1. **Skill Documents** (in `/home/travis/environment/skills/`):
   - `maven-java-version-compatibility.md` - Covers tools.jar issues
   - `git-diff-format.md` - Covers unified diff format
   - `maven-dependency-management.md` - Covers Maven dependency management

2. **Analysis Document**:
   - `/home/travis/build/failed/failed_reasons.txt` - Documents all errors and solutions

3. **Patch Files** (in `/home/travis/build/failed/google/auto/`):
   - `patch_1.diff` - common/pom.xml: compile-testing 0.7 → 0.19
   - `patch_2.diff` - service/pom.xml: compile-testing 0.6 → 0.19
   - `patch_3.diff` - value/pom.xml: compile-testing 0.6 → 0.19
   - `patch_4.diff` - factory/pom.xml: compile-testing 0.8 → 0.19
   - `patch_5.diff` - factory/pom.xml: Add javax.annotation-api 1.3.2
   - `patch_6.diff` - value/pom.xml: Add javax.annotation-api 1.3.2

### Verification

All four modules (common, service, factory, value) now compile successfully with `mvn compile -DskipTests`.
